architecture.mechanism: Data-driven steering dynamics modeling combined with steering angle tracking control (PID and neural), which learns nominal vehicle response and characterizes direction asymmetry in closed-loop tracking, enabling detection and compensation of abnormal directional behavior.
architecture.intervention: Embed the data-driven steering dynamics model and PID/neural tracking controller into the Nissan passenger car's electronic control system so it continuously compares live steering and drivetrain response against the learned nominal model; when a loose engine computer wire causes signal dropout or drift, the resulting tracking error and direction asymmetry are detected and the controller compensates the steering/gear command to maintain safe operation and trigger a safe-state fallback.
architecture.expected_effect: The wire-fault-induced deviation is absorbed by closed-loop tracking, eliminating sudden deceleration and steering pull while keeping the vehicle operable even without a dashboard warning.
architecture.falsification_test: On a test vehicle, introduce an intermittent open-circuit in the engine computer wire harness while driving at 35–45 mph; measure steering angle tracking RMSE and lateral pull. If RMSE remains near the characterized 1.23° level and no deceleration or pull occurs, the mechanism works; if the fault produces uncompensated pull or gear failure, it is falsified.
